title: Germanwings v Henning (Case C-452/13), 4 September 2014
excerpt: the concept of ‘arrival time’, which is used to determine the length of the delay to which passengers on a flight have been subject, refers to the time at which at least one of the doors of the aircraft is opened, the assumption being that, at that moment, the passengers are permitted to leave the aircraft.
summary: Arrival time is when at least one aircraft door opens.
